statusNote: Small private, for-profit, online-focused institution (also referred to by its Rosslyn, VA address). Founding president has led the institution continuously since inception; no other presidents on record.

leaders.notes: Founding president since UMT's creation in 1998; a naturalized U.S. citizen and former visiting scholar at George Washington University / International Fellow at the Smithsonian. From 2010 she was the subject of a years-long FBI investigation into her immigration paperwork and alleged ties to the Chinese military; prosecutors ultimately filed no charges, and she later sued the FBI/DOJ/DOD/DHS over leaks of the investigation to Fox News. She has remained UMT president throughout.

statusNote: Not a separately-led degree-granting institution for most of the 1996+ window: from 1958 through the mid-2000s this was a division of Chapman University (Division of Residence Education Centers, then the College of Lifelong Learning, renamed Chapman University College in 2001), overseen by a Dean (e.g., Dr. Karen Graham) rather than its own chief executive, and reported to Chapman University's own president. It became a separately accredited institution led by its own chancellor around 2008-2009 when it was renamed Brandman University (funded by a gift from the Joyce and Saul Brandman Foundation). In September 2021 the University of Massachusetts and Chapman University transferred control of Brandman University to UMass, and it was rebranded University of Massachusetts Global -- a nonprofit affiliate of the UMass system rather than one of its traditional public campuses. Leaders below are listed from the point (2007-2009) it gained its own chancellor.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President for Finance and Administration and Chief Operating Officer
leaders.notes: Joined as chancellor of what was then Chapman University College in 2007 and became founding chancellor of Brandman University when it was separately established/renamed in 2009; led the institution through its 2021 transfer to UMass and rebrand as UMass Global. Retired effective September 1, 2022.

Served as President of National University 2016-2021 before joining UMass Global; began as interim chancellor in May 2022 and was formally appointed permanent chancellor in June 2022, the first new chancellor since the UMass acquisition. Still serving.
